questions.question: When Shanu was asked his age then he being good in arithmetic reasoning said that 5 years before he was one-twentieth of his fathers present age. 12 years afterwards he said he will get married and his wife’s age will be three times his present age. After 2 years of marriage, he shall get a baby and the average age of the family will become 18.5 years. What will be Shanu's fathers age when he gets the baby?
questions.explanation:
Let 5 years ago the age of shanu be \(m\)

At present Shanu’s fathers age = \(20m\)

12 years hence, shanu’s age = \(m + 5 + 12 = m + 17\)

And his wife’s age = \((m + 5) \times 3 = 3m + 15\)

After 2 years of marriage, Shanu’s age = \(17 + m + 2 = \ 19 + m\)

Now, Shanu’s fathers age= \(20m + 12 + 2 = 20m + 14\) years

Shanu’s wife’s age = \(3m + 15 + 2 = 3m + 17\)

Shanu’s baby’s age = 0 years

The average of all will be:

\(19 + m + 20m + 14 + 17 + 3m + 0 = \ 18.5 \times 4 = 74\)

\(\Rightarrow \ 24m = 24\)

\(\Rightarrow m = 1\)

Shanu;s fathers age when he gets the baby will be = 20×1 + 14 = 34

Hence, the correct option is 4th option.

All of three started the work together but only 'P' worked for last (x - 8) days. (III) (0.5x + 2) days

Number of days taken by 'P' to complete the work = 80 days

Number of days taken by 'Q' to complete the same work = 80 - 20 = 60 days

Ratio of efficiency of 'Q' to 'R' = 5 : 4

Ratio of time taken to complete the work (by 'Q' to 'R') = 4 : 5

Number of days taken by 'R' to complete the same work = (60/4) × 5 = 75 days

Let the total work = LCM of 80, 60 and 75 = 1200 units

Efficiency of P : Q : R =1200/80 : 1200/60 : 1200/75 = 15 : 20 : 16

All of three started the work together but only 'P' worked for last (x - 8) days. If the total work gets completed in (2x - 8) days.

Therefore, (15 + 20 + 16) × [(2x - 8) - (x - 8)] + 15 × (x - 8) = 1200

⇒ 51x + 15x = 1200 + 120

⇒ 66x = 1320

⇒ x = 20

• Time taken to cross a bridge is 24 seconds.
• The train also crosses a pole in some seconds.
• We have to choose the correct pair of values for bridge length and pole crossing time from the given options.

Calculation:

So, the length of the bridge = 20 × 24 – 160 = 320

480 – 160 = 320

320 = 320

So, option A can be the answer.

For option B:

Length of the train = 20 × 10 = 200 m

So, the length of the bridge = 20 × 24 – 200 = 280

480 – 200 = 280

280 = 280

So, option B can be the answer.

Length of the train = 20 × 11 = 220 m

So, the length of the bridge = 20 × 24 – 220 = 250

480 – 220 = 250

260 ≠ 250

So, option C can’t be the answer.

Hence, the correct option is C.

• When a train crosses a bridge, distance covered equals length of train plus length of bridge.

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, two quantities I and II are given. Compare quantity I and quantity II on its basis. (Only quantity is to be considered)

Train A crosses train B in 13 seconds while running in the opposite direction and train C crosses train A in 100 seconds while running in the same direction. Average speed of trains A and B is 15 m/s and the speed of train C is 4 m/s more than that of train A. Train A can cross a 140 m long platform in 20 seconds and the speed of train B is 14 m/s.

Quantity I: If speed of train C were 95% of its original speed, then in what time train C would cross train B while running in the same direction?

Quantity II: If a series is formed, whose 1st term is the length of train A, 2nd term is (1st term - \(2^{2}\)), 3rd term is (2nd term - \(3^{2}\)), 4th term is (3rd term - \(5^{2}\)) and 5th term is (4th term - \(7^{2}\)), then what is the 5th term of the series?
options: Quantity I = Quantity II or relation can’t be established
questions.explanation:
The speed of train B = 14 m/s

So, the speed of train A = 2 × 15 - 14 = 16 m/s

And the speed of train C = 16 + 4 = 20 m/s

Let the lengths of trains A, B and C are ‘a’ m, ‘b’ m and ‘c’ m respectively.

Since, train A crosses train B in 13 seconds while running in the opposite direction.

So,

\(\frac{a\  + \ b}{16\  + \ 14}\  = \ 13\)

a + b = 390 —-------(1)

Since, train C crosses train A in 100 seconds while running in the same direction.

So,

\(\frac{a\  + \ c}{20\  - \ 16}\  = \ 100\)

a + c = 400 —-------(2)

Since, train A can cross a 140 m long platform in 20 seconds.

So,

\(\frac{a\  + \ 140}{16}\  = \ 20\)

a = 180

From equation (1):

b = 210

From equation (2):

c = 220

Quantity I:

Since, original speed of train C = 20 m/s

So, new speed of train C would be = 95% of 20 = 19 m/s

And the time taken by train C to cross train B while running in the same direction would be = \(\frac{210\  + \ 220}{19\  - \ 14}\) = 86 seconds

Quantity II:

1st term of the series = 180

2nd term of the series = 180 - \(2^{2}\) = 176

3rd term of the series = 176 - \(3^{2}\) = 167

4th term of the series = 167 - \(5^{2}\) = 142

5th term of the series = 142 - \(7^{2}\) = 93

Hence, Quantity I < Quantity II

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, three quantities I, II and III are given. Compare quantity I, quantity II and quantity III on its basis. (Only quantity is to be considered)

Two equations (a) and (b) are given below:

(a): 3x - 4y = 2

(b): x - 2y = 8

Quantity I: Find the value of ‘x’ by solving both the equations?

Quantity II: Find the value of ‘y’ by solving both the equations?

Quantity III: An article is marked up by ₹250 and sold by giving a discount of ₹200 on marked price. If the marked up percent is P%, discount given is Q% and marked price of the article is ₹1000, then find the value of (Q - P)?
questions.explanation:
3x - 4y = 2 —---------(a)

x - 2y = 8 —---------(b)

By equation (a) - equation (b) × 2:

3x - 4y - 2x + 4y = 2 - 16

x = -14

From equation (b):

y = -11

Quantity I:

Value of ‘x’ = -14

Quantity II:

Value of ‘y’ = -11

Quantity III:

Since MP of the article = ₹1000

So, CP of the article = 1000 - 250 = ₹750

And SP of the article = 1000 - 200 = ₹800

Now,

P = \(\frac{250}{750}\  \times \ 100\  = \ 33\frac{1}{3}\%\)

And,

Q = \(\frac{200}{1000}\  \times \ 100\  = \ 20\%\)

So, value of (Q - P) = 20 - \(33\frac{1}{3}\) = -\(13\frac{1}{3}\)

Hence, Quantity II > Quantity III > Quantity I

questions.question:

Two series A and B are given below with one wrong term in series.

A: 3, 8, 24, 45, 120, 168

B: 28, 42, 56, 98, 154, 182

Quantity I: Find the average of wrong terms of both the series?

Quantity II: Find the difference between the next term of series A and the next term of series B?
options: Quantity I = Quantity II or No relation

Logic in series A:

\(2^{2}\) - 1 = 3

\(3^{2}\) - 1 = 8

\(5^{2}\) - 1 = 24

\(7^{2}\) - 1 = 48(45)

\(11^{2}\) - 1 = 120

\(13^{2}\) - 1 = 168

So, wrong term of the series = 45

And the next term of the series = \(17^{2}\) - 1 = 288

Logic in series B:

14 × 2 = 28

14 × 3 = 42

14 × 5 = 70(56)

14 × 7 = 98

14 × 11 = 154

14 × 13 = 182

So, wrong term of the series = 56

And the next term of the series = 14 × 17 = 238

Quantity I:

Average of wrong terms of both the series = \(\frac{45\  + \ 56}{2}\) = 50.5

Quantity II:

Difference between next terms of both the series = 288 - 238 = 50

Hence, Quantity I > Quantity II

Directions: In the question given below, three sentences are given, each of which has two words highlighted in bold. Choose the word in each sentence that fits appropriately in the context, and select the right option.

questions.explanation:
lurid vs lucid

Lurid: sensational, shocking, or vividly gruesome — usually used in a negative sense (e.g., lurid headlines).
Lucid: clear and easy to understand — often used to describe communication or thought.
The sentence praises the professor’s clear explanation of complex topics, which suits the meaning of lucid.
Correct: B (lucid)

Navigate vs negotiate

Navigate: to steer, guide, or find a way through, especially in literal or figurative travel.
Negotiate: to discuss or bargain to reach an agreement.
The sentence describes a ship making its way safely through a rocky passage — a physical movement, not a discussion. So, navigate is the right choice.
Correct: A (navigate)

mischievous vs meticulous

Mischievous: playful in a naughty or troublesome way.
Meticulous: extremely careful and precise, with great attention to detail.
The sentence highlights admiration for someone's detailed focus, which matches meticulous, not playful, behavior.
Correct: B (meticulous)

Thus, the correct answer is option (D).

Correct: B (systematic)

Thus, the correct answer is option (B).

questions.explanation:

questions.question: Which of the following can be a suitable title to the given passage?
options: Angela Merkel: The Longest-Serving Chancellor of Germany
Merkel's Pragmatic Leadership in a Changing Europe
The Enduring Influence of Angela Merkel's Leadership
questions.explanation:
"Angela Merkel: The Longest-Serving Chancellor of Germany" is the most suitable title for the passage because it directly highlights the central theme of the text, which is Angela Merkel's remarkable tenure as the Chancellor of Germany and her significant contributions to the country and the world. The passage discusses her accomplishments, her leadership style, her handling of various crises, and her impact on global politics during her lengthy time in office. Therefore, this title accurately summarizes the content of the passage and provides a clear focus for the reader. Hence, option B is the correct choice.

Option (A) "A Quiet Giant: Angela Merkel's Legacy" - While this option captures the idea of Angela Merkel's legacy and leadership style being quiet and understated, it doesn't emphasize her lengthy tenure as Chancellor, which is a significant aspect of the passage.

Option (C) "Merkel's Pragmatic Leadership in a Changing Europe" - This option focuses on her leadership style, but it doesn't highlight the fact that she served as the longest-serving Chancellor of Germany, which is a key point in the passage.

Option (D) "Angela Merkel's Impact on Global Politics" - This title is too broad and doesn't specifically highlight her record as the longest-serving Chancellor of Germany, which is the primary focus of the passage.

Option (E) "The Enduring Influence of Angela Merkel's Leadership" - While this option suggests the lasting impact of Merkel's leadership, it doesn't specifically mention her lengthy tenure or her status as the longest-serving Chancellor, which is a significant aspect of the passage.

The passage talks about how human energy consumption is increasing exponentially, especially with the advent of AI and cryptocurrency.
